name: researcher
description: Answers one question by fanning three scouts across it in parallel. A Legion rather than a Court - the scouts are interchangeable, and are bound to three different models on purpose.

king.role: split the question into independent threads, then synthesise three reports into one answer

scout-a.role: answer one independent thread of the question and report only what was found

scout-b.role: answer one independent thread of the question and report only what was found

scout-c.role: answer one independent thread of the question and report only what was found

routing: a question with three or more independent threads -> split it and fan to @scout-a, @scout-b and @scout-c in one turn
a question with a single thread -> @scout-a alone, do not fan; parallelism costs quota
threads that depend on each other's answers -> run them in sequence, not in parallel
synthesis, contradictions between reports, what it all means -> keep it yourself

discipline.scout-a: cheap - one thread, one report, no speculation beyond what was read
discipline.scout-b: cheap - one thread, one report, no speculation beyond what was read
discipline.scout-c: cheap - one thread, one report, no speculation beyond what was read
discipline.self: three scouts are bound to three DIFFERENT models deliberately. If Zen's daily bucket is per-model that is three independent budgets; if it is shared, this costs nothing extra. Never bind a parallel head to Zhipu - it is single-concurrent by contract
